name: Monocacy National Battlefield
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Monocacy National Battlefield near Frederick, Maryland, preserves the site of the Battle of Monocacy, fought on July 9, 1864 — often called "The Battle That Saved Washington." When Confederate General Jubal Early led an army toward the Union capital, a hastily assembled force of Union soldiers under General Lew Wallace (later the author of "Ben-Hur") delayed Early's advance for an entire day at the Monocacy River crossing. Although the Union forces were defeated, the delay allowed reinforcements to reach Washington's defenses in time to prevent the capital's capture. The battlefield was established as a national battlefield in 1934 and preserves 1,647 acres of agricultural landscape and historic structures.
